text: dsh-skill-switch 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 的 Windows 技能管理插件，在 DSH 设置页提供 Skills 页面。它扫描中央目录中的 SKILL.md 技能包，展示状态并支持搜索筛选、单项启停、批量停用和修改来源路径。启用时在 DSH skills 目录建立 Junction，停用前核对链接身份，已有外部目标会显示为冲突。适合希望选择性管理全局 DSH Skills 的 Windows 用户；默认目录为 ~/.cc-switch/skills，无需 API Key。

dsh-skill-switch adds a Skills page to DSH Settings. It scans a central folder for SKILL.md bundles and lets users search and toggle global skills. Enabling creates a Junction in DSH skills; existing targets appear as conflicts. For Windows users; default source: ~/.cc-switch/skills.
想从一个公共目录挑选哪些全局 Skill 出现在 DSH 里。
能在设置页面搜索并启用某个本地 Skill 吗？
让 DSH 只加载我选中的全局技能目录项目。
我想调整插件扫描技能包的中央文件夹位置。
DSH 里同名技能发生冲突时，怎样查看状态并避免覆盖原有目录？
需要一次关闭所有由中央技能目录启用的项目。
I want to selectively expose global skills from one folder in DSH.
How can I find and toggle a skill from the DSH settings page?
dsh-skill-switch 的功能「扫描技能目录」：读取中央目录的直接子目录并解析其中 SKILL.md 的 YAML frontmatter，以名称和描述列出有效技能，同时标出格式错误或重复名称。
dsh-skill-switch 的功能「选择性启用」：在设置页搜索、筛选技能并切换单项；主机为有效技能在 DSH skills 目录创建 Junction，并登记其来源与链接身份。
dsh-skill-switch 的功能「停用与状态核验」：停用单项或批量停用已管理技能；移除前会验证 Junction 身份和目的路径，外部目标以冲突状态展示。
dsh-skill-switch 的功能「更改技能来源目录」：用户在设置页编辑中央目录路径并保存；路径需符合 Windows 绝对路径或波浪号开头的格式，且不能与 DSH 技能目标目录互相包含。
dsh-skill-switch 的功能「平台状态提示」：在非 Windows 平台返回 unsupported-platform 状态，设置页面显示提示并禁用目录修改和技能切换操作。
dsh-skill-switch 仅在 Windows 创建 Junction；其他平台报告 unsupported-platform，且不执行文件变更（src/manager.ts:79-90）。

dsh-skill-switch README · dsh-skill-switch：English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Windows-only Skill management for DeepSeek Harness Web. The plugin scans one central directory and selectively exposes user-global Skills in `$DSH_HOME/skills` through directory Junctions.

The default central directory is `~/.cc-switch/skills`. Version `0.2.0` targets DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`.

dsh-skill-switch README · Scope：- Manages user-global DSH Skills only.
- Accepts direct `<directory>/SKILL.md` directory bundles and identifies them by frontmatter name.
- Creates and removes Windows Junctions only.
- Never installs, updates, edits, or deletes central Skills.
- Never adopts existing files, directories, or links in `$DSH_HOME/skills`.
- Does not manage project Skills or other agents.

dsh-skill-switch README · Install：Install a reviewed commit into a DSH profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:hzthzt/dsh-skill-switch#<commit-sha>
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config
dsh --profile <profile> web
```

The repository commits `lib/`, so Git installation does not need to run a build script. A local tarball can be installed instead:

```sh
pnpm pack
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-skill-switch-0.2.0.tgz
```

dsh-skill-switch README · Install：The plugin pins its DSH peers to the exact baseline version. If the running harness does not match, DSH skips the bundle (the Skills section simply does not appear); either re-baseline this repository or accept the mismatch explicitly with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version dsh-skill-switch@0.2.0 --dsh-version <running> --accept-risk`.

Open DSH Settings and select **Skills**.

dsh-skill-switch README · Skill format：The central directory is scanned one level deep. Source directory links and linked `SKILL.md` files are ignored. A source directory may use any name; the `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name` is the canonical Skill identity and must be kebab-case:

```text
central-directory/
`-- example-skill-main/
    `-- SKILL.md
```

```yaml
---
name: example-skill
description: A non-empty description.
---

dsh-skill-switch README · Skill format：Enabling this example creates `$DSH_HOME/skills/example-skill`, which points to `central-directory/example-skill-main`. If multiple valid source directories declare the same frontmatter name, every duplicate is reported as invalid until the ambiguity is removed.

The configured central path must be a Windows absolute path or start with `~`. Environment-variable expressions such as `%USERPROFILE%` are not expanded. The central directory and `$DSH_HOME/skills` cannot contain one another.

dsh-skill-switch README · States：| State | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | Valid central Skill with no target entry | Can be enabled |
| `enabled` | Junction is owned and verified by this plugin | Can be disabled |
| `conflict` | An external target already uses the same name | Read-only |
| `invalid` | The Skill file/frontmatter is invalid, or multiple sources declare the same name | Read-only unless already managed |
| `broken` | The managed source disappeared or no longer declares the recorded Skill | Can be disabled safely |

dsh-skill-switch README · States：Existing ordinary directories such as `~/.dsh/skills/nai-fadian` remain externally managed. A same-named central Skill is reported as a conflict and its toggle is disabled.

dsh-skill-switch README · Safety model：Ownership records are stored in `$DSH_HOME/skill-switch/manifest.json`, and the configured central directory in `$DSH_HOME/skill-switch/config.json`. Both documents are versioned, strictly validated, and replaced atomically. Every manifest record includes the source and filesystem identity of the Junction created by this plugin.

dsh-skill-switch README · Safety model：Before removal, the plugin validates the Skill name, recomputes the target under `$DSH_HOME/skills`, verifies that the target is still a link with the recorded identity, and verifies its destination. A missing target is pruned from the manifest. A replaced target loses ownership and is displayed as external. A managed Skill is matched by both its frontmatter name and recorded source path, so moving a source requires disabling it before the new path can be enabled. Source Skills are never removed.

dsh-skill-switch README · Safety model：All scans and mutations share one serial queue. Changing the central directory is refused while any verified managed Junction remains; use **Disable all** first. On non-Windows hosts, the Remote returns `unsupported-platform` and performs no filesystem mutation.

dsh-skill-switch README · Development：Use Node.js 24 and `pnpm@11.7.0`:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

The build runs the pinned Typert generator and commits `lib/` artifacts intentionally. Windows tests use real Junctions; the Ubuntu test job verifies build behavior and the explicit unsupported-platform result.
